# apps/cli/test/fixtures/read-only-shapes.txt
#
# Every command spelling the five D-073 review rounds on SCP-355 (#706-#709) drove
# against the interview's guard, collected into one place so the oracle test
# (interview-oracle.test.ts) holds them permanently: whatever this file admits is
# proven, by a real shell, to write, change or delete nothing and run no marker.
# One command per line, a line starting with # is a comment naming the group below
# it, and blank lines are ignored. Each command line is a JSON string literal, not
# raw shell text — several of these commands carry a real newline (a here-document
# needs one to mean anything), which JSON.parse reads back correctly and a raw line
# could not hold at all.

# a coprocess: the command stands past the keyword, inside a body as much as outside one
"cat \"$(coproc git log --output=x)\""
"cat \"$(coproc { git log --output=x; })\""
"cat \"$(coproc W { git log --output=x; })\""
"cat \"$(true; coproc git log --output=x)\""
"cat <(coproc git log --output=x)"

# the adversarial sweep against c24917e3 (adv355) — every distinct shape
# it drove, kept so the oracle re-runs each admitted one under a real shell.
# adv: subst
"cat \"$(program)\""
"cat \"$(p)\""
"cat \"$(evil.sh)\""
"cat $(program)"
"ls \"$(program)\""
"wc \"$(program)\""

# adv: subst-wrap
"cat \"$(sh -c 'evil.sh')\""
"cat \"$(sh evil.sh)\""
"cat \"$(bash -c 'program')\""
"cat \"$(bash evil.sh)\""
"cat \"$(zsh -c 'program')\""
"cat \"$(env program)\""
"cat \"$(env -i program)\""
"cat \"$(command program)\""
"cat \"$(command -p program)\""
"cat \"$(nice program)\""
"cat \"$(nice -n 1 program)\""
"cat \"$(nohup program)\""
"cat \"$(exec program)\""
"cat \"$(builtin program)\""
"cat \"$(time program)\""
"cat \"$(xargs program </dev/null)\""
"cat \"$(eval program)\""
"cat \"$(eval 'program')\""
"cat \"$(/bin/sh -c program)\""
# adv: backtick
"cat \"`program`\""
"cat `program`"
"cat \"`sh -c 'evil.sh'`\""
# adv: nested
"cat \"$(echo $(program))\""
"cat \"$(cat $(program))\""

# the top-level class closed this pass — a function body, an assignment
# prefix or a bare environment assignment that runs a program past the one
# it names (SCP-355). Each is refused; the two whose var is itself a
# read-only command name are inert and admitted, and run nothing but a read.
"cat () { evil.sh; }; cat"
"cat(){ evil.sh; }; cat README.md"
"ls () ( evil.sh ); ls"
"cat=1 program"
"PATH=/tmp/evil:$PATH; ls"
"PATH=/tmp/evil ls"
"IFS=x; ls"
"A=1 B=2 program"
"f(){ evil.sh; }; f"
"cat \"$(cat=1 program)\""
"cat \"$(f(){ evil.sh; }; f)\""
"cat \"$(PATH=/tmp/evil ls)\""
"cat=1 ls"
"find=1 find . -name x"

# the adversarial round (adv355b) — an escaped or quoted paren inside a
# substitution body must not end the body early, so a program hidden past it
# (cat $(cat \) ; evil.sh)) is read and refused, not left in the prefix a bare
# paren count would stop at. All refused; the oracle re-runs any it admits.
"cat $(cat \\) ; evil.sh)"
"cat \"$(cat \\) ; evil.sh)\""
"ls $(ls \\) ; program)"
"wc $(wc \\) ; evil.sh)"
"cat <(cat \\) ; program)"
"tee >(cat \\) ; evil.sh) < /dev/null"
"cat `cat \\` ; evil.sh`"
"cat \"`cat \\` ; evil.sh`\""
"cat $(cat ')' ; evil.sh)"
"cat $(echo \")\" ; evil.sh)"
"cat $(echo $(cat \\) ; evil.sh))"
"cat $(cat \\) ; cat $(evil.sh))"
"cat <<E\n$(cat \\) ; evil.sh)\nE"
"cat <<-E\n\t$(cat \\) ; evil.sh)\nE"
"cat <<< $(cat \\) ; evil.sh)"
"cat $(cat \"\\)\" ; evil.sh)"
"cat $(cat \\) ; git rm -f tracked.txt)"
"grep x $(cat \\) ; evil.sh)"

# adv355b round two — a nested backtick (`\``) inside a backtick substitution
# opens a nested command bash runs; a reader that stops at the first backtick
# misses it. All refused; the oracle re-runs any it admits.
"cat `cat \\`evil.sh\\``"
"cat \"`cat \\`evil.sh\\``\""
"cat `sh -c \\`evil.sh\\``"
"cat `cat \\`rm tracked.txt\\``"
"cat `cat \\`touch ../ESCAPED\\``"
"git show `cat \\`evil.sh\\``"
"cat $(cat `evil.sh`)"
"cat `cat \\`program a b c\\``"
"wc `cat \\`evil.sh\\``"
"cat `cat \\`cat \\\\\\`evil.sh\\\\\\`\\``"

# adv355b round three — every here-document a line opens takes its body in
# order; a second `<<B` on the same line is expanded too, so a substitution in
# its body runs. Refused (a quoted delimiter's body stays literal and inert).
"cat <<A <<B\nhello\nA\n$(evil.sh)\nB"
"cat <<A <<B\nx\nA\n$(rm tracked.txt)\nB"
"cat <<A <<B\nx\nA\n$(git log --output=x)\nB"
"cat <<A <<B\nx\nA\n$(find . -delete)\nB"
"cat <<A <<B <<C\n1\nA\n2\nB\n$(evil.sh)\nC"
"cat <<-A <<-B\n\t1\n\tA\n\t$(evil.sh)\n\tB"
"cat <<A <<B\n$(evil.sh)\nA\nhello\nB"
"cat <<'E'\n$(evil.sh)\nE"
"cat <<A <<B\n$(git ls-files)\nA\n$(git status --short)\nB"
